tanaka: Heads up - encountered a subtle auth/rotation thing when running the python sample app behind our dev proxy. After rotating keys, requests started 403'ing only in the proxy path.

jess: which SDK and sample? py or js?
\jtanaka: python sdk v0.9.2 and sample-app/python/server.py. No issues calling API directly. Proxy logs show it strips REDWOOD_PROJECT header and adds X-Local-Auth.

omar: pattern sounds familiar. Our SDKs have slightly different env precedence: js prefers constructor arg > env > headers, py did env > headers > constructor (bug). That can make rotated keys behave oddly if the proxy injects header.
\jess: oh that mismatch could explain parity bugs for new devs. We aim for constructor > env > explicit headers (X-Project-Id) > local-proxy header.
	li: can you paste the minimal repro and logs?
\jtanaka: repro: 
```
# rotate locally
export REDWOOD_API_KEY=sk.rotated.2026
export REDWOOD_PROJECT=team-blue
python sample-app/server.py --use-proxy
curl -v http://localhost:8080/api/run
```
proxy snippet: 
```
-> POST /v1/completions
Host: api.redwood.internal
X-Forwarded-For: 127.0.0.1
X-Local-Auth: project=team-blue;key=rotated
# note: X-Project-Id is missing
```
Response: `403 Forbidden - project header missing` from service side.

omar: because py SDK read REDWOOD_PROJECT from env but when proxy rewrote requests it removed header and the client started including only X-Local-Auth and the server rejected unscoped key.
	jess: two actionable items: (1) make py SDK auth precedence match spec (constructor > env > headers > local-auth), (2) update sample-app to always add `X-Project-Id` when proxy mode is on.
	li: add (3) log a non-fatal warning when a rotated key is detected and header parsing fails in dev mode. don't change production behaviour. maybe an env gate like `REDWOOD_DEV_AUTH_STRICT=1`.
\jtanaka: agreed, I can PR both the sample-app tweak and sdk-py fix. Also will add unit tests: header-missing, local-auth-malformed, and constructor-override.
	omar: small thought: SDKs should normalize env var names across languages. We had `REDWOOD_ORG` vs `REDWOOD_TEAM` confusion in internal examples. Let's standardize on `REDWOOD_ORG` + `REDWOOD_PROJECT` for scoping and update onboarding docs.
	jess: yes please. And include a short paragraph in the quickstart: "If you run a local proxy, ensure it forwards X-Project-Id or use constructor arg to avoid header rewriting issues."
	ci-bot: CI pipeline: sdk-py/unit-tests queued for tanaka/py-auth-fallback branch.
	li: also add an e2e flakiness note — our CI runs proxy tests in parallel and sometimes envs bleed between tests causing false rotation failures. Add an isolated integration fixture to avoid env leaking.
\jtanaka: noted, will add fixture. PR draft: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk-py/pull/210 (WIP)
	jess: thanks. Once the SDK parity change is merged, let's run a quick smoke across js/py/ruby samples to confirm consistent precedence and messages.
	omaar: tiny nit: spell out header names in docs: `X-Project-Id`, `X-Org-Id`, `X-Local-Auth` so infra team can config proxies correctly.
	li: can we also add a dev-only telemetry ping when parsing local-auth so we can detect how many teams rely on proxy-injected auth? opt-out by default.
\jtanaka: good idea but opt-in only. I'll mention that in PR.
	jess: awesome - thanks for triage. Ping when PR is ready and I'll kick off smoke tests. :rocket:
